_meta.description: Key financials for all 38 GSE-listed companies, refreshed from live web research (FY2024-FY2025 results, some post-IPO/post-recapitalisation corrections). Revenue and profit in millions of the stated currency field (mostly GHS; some cross-listed/foreign-domiciled names report in USD, GMD or AUD — check currency per entry). Several entries also corrected prior data errors (wrong company identity, wrong currency, wrong share count) found during this refresh — see each analystNote for details. dataQuality reflects how much of each entry was independently reverified vs carried over from the prior stale baseline.
_meta.note: This baseline is a snapshot from FY2024/FY2025 annual results as of Aug 2026 research and will go stale again over time. The app also fetches live interim/half-year and newer annual PDFs at request time (see gseReports.js) which should be treated as more current than this static file when both are present.

keyStrengths: Largest telecom in Ghana with dominant mobile/data market share
FY2025 service revenue +36.2% to GHS24.4bn and PAT +55.9% to GHS7.8bn — record year
MTN Group backing — capital, technology and brand support
Fintech arm (MoMo) revenue up 35.7% to GHS6.0bn, a major growth driver
keyRisks: Currency devaluation increases USD-denominated costs (roaming, equipment)
Regulatory risk from NCA (National Communications Authority)
Competition from Telecel (formerly Vodafone Ghana) and AirtelTigo
MTNGH.GH.analystNote: FY2025 audited results: service revenue GHS24.4bn (+36.2%), EBITDA GHS14.7bn (margin 60.1%), PAT GHS7.8bn (+55.9%), EPS GHS0.592. Total FY2025 dividend GHS0.48/share (81% payout ratio), including a final GHS0.40. Shares outstanding confirmed at ~13.24 billion via a 2026 AGM notice — a large increase versus previously assumed figures, likely reflecting a corrected/updated float count rather than a real per-share dilution event (netProfit/shares reconciles cleanly to the reported EPS). operatingMargin, roe, roa, debtToEquity and currentRatio are carried over from older data and were not independently reverified this cycle.

keyStrengths: Ghana's largest indigenous bank with 60+ years of history
FY2025 record year: operating income +40.9% to GHS6.3bn, PBT +67.4% to GHS3.17bn, ROE 39.0%
Dividend resumed at GHS1.00/share after a 5-year Bank of Ghana-driven suspension
Extensive branch/ATM network and strong retail/SME franchise
keyRisks: Public-sector salary payment dependency exposes it to government payment timing
Currency risk on USD-denominated liabilities
Dividend track record was interrupted for 5 years (2021-2024) — resumption is recent, not yet a long consistent streak
GCB.GH.analystNote: FY2025 audited results are the strongest in the bank's recent history: operating income GHS6.3bn (+40.9%), PBT GHS3.17bn (+67.4%), net profit ~GHS2.06bn, EPS GHS7.78, ROE 39.0%. Post-DDEP recovery appears essentially complete. Dividend of GHS1.00/share (total payout ~GHS265m) was approved at the April 2026 AGM, ending a 5-year suspension — dividendHistory downgraded from 'Consistent' to 'Irregular' to reflect that gap. currentRatio, debtToEquity and roa (roa here is a rough netProfit/total-assets estimate) were not independently reverified.

keyStrengths: Confirmed recovery: FY2024 PBT of GHS414.2m vs a GHS946.2m loss in 2023
Strong digital banking platform (Cal Mobile)
Deposits grew 29% to GHS9.6bn; ~GHS792m in impaired-loan recoveries during 2024
keyRisks: Dividend remains suspended despite return to profit
CalBank completed a large ~GHS600m rights issue in 2024, materially diluting shareholders — public sources conflict on the resulting exact share count (reports range from ~2.5bn to ~4.2bn shares)
Capital adequacy still recovering; NPL and concentration risk remain
CAL.GH.analystNote: FY2024 audited results confirm a real recovery: revenue ~GHS996m, PBT GHS414.2m, net profit after tax ~GHS268m (vs prior-year loss). However, EPS, shares outstanding, ROE, ROA, debt-to-equity and current ratio could NOT be independently reverified this cycle — the 2024 rights issue makes the true post-raise share count uncertain in public sources, so these fields are carried over from stale data and should be treated as approximate until confirmed from CalBank's primary annual report.

keyStrengths: Backed by Ecobank Transnational — pan-African brand and capital
FY2025: revenue +12.2% to GHS4.86bn, PAT +7.2% to GHS1.82bn, ROE 29.0%, cost-to-income improved to 35.1%
Strong fee/commission and trading income growth offsetting a sharp net-interest-income decline
Well-capitalised relative to local peers
keyRisks: Net interest income fell ~29% YoY (GHS3.77bn to GHS2.68bn) as rates/cedi stabilised — future NII growth is less certain
Parent (ETI) has had its own capital pressures
Currency risk on USD liabilities
EGH.GH.analystNote: FY2025 audited results (KPMG, unmodified opinion): revenue GHS4.86bn, PAT GHS1.82bn, EPS GHS5.65, ROE 29.0%, ROA 3.9%. Final dividend of GHS1.21/share was declared for payment in July 2026 — an earlier interim tranche may also have been paid during 2025, so the true full-year total dividend could be somewhat higher than the figure shown. Shares outstanding (~323m) cross-validate cleanly against netProfit/EPS. currentRatio and debtToEquity are carried over from stale data, not reverified.

keyStrengths: International bank with Standard Chartered Group backing and standards
FY2025: operating income +2% to GHS1.84bn, net income +12.3% to GHS804.2m, EPS GHS5.96
Capital Adequacy Ratio improved to 27.45% (from 24.01%) — best-in-class among GSE banks
Trading income surged (GHS555.1m vs GHS149.4m) offsetting an interest-income decline
keyRisks: Net interest income fell over 28% as the cedi stabilised and rates eased — growth increasingly reliant on trading income, which is less predictable
Limited retail banking presence vs. GCB and Ecobank
StanChart Group strategic repositioning could affect Ghana focus
SCB.GH.analystNote: FY2025 results (EY audited, unmodified opinion) show continued high-quality earnings: operating income GHS1.84bn, net income GHS804.2m (+12.3%), EPS GHS5.96, CAR 27.45%. A dividend of approximately GHS5.00/share is implied by an aggregate GHS673.48m payout announced at the August 2026 (56th) AGM divided by ~134.76m shares outstanding — treat this as an approximation pending confirmation of the exact declared per-share rate. Shares outstanding (~135m) is a material update from previously assumed figures. roe, roa, currentRatio and debtToEquity are carried over from stale data, not reverified.

keyStrengths: Preference share — fixed preferential dividend ahead of ordinary shareholders
Standard Chartered Bank Ghana backing — low default risk, and SCB.GH's FY2025 results were strong (see SCB.GH entry)
Income security higher than ordinary equity
keyRisks: No capital appreciation (fixed-income like instrument)
Dividend could be suspended if bank faces distress
Interest rate risk — value falls if market rates rise
SCBPREF.GH.analystNote: Public reporting on the preference dividend is fragmented across multiple partial announcements: a tranche of GHS0.0512/share was reported for the six months to September 2025, and a separate declaration cited GHS0.1689/share; dps here uses the higher, more recent figure (~GHS0.17) as the best approximate full-year rate, up from the prior GHS0.08 baseline, but the precise interim/final split could not be confirmed. This remains a fixed-income-like instrument; suitable for income-focused investors only.

keyStrengths: Backed by Access Bank Nigeria (one of Africa's largest banks)
Customer deposits continued growing (GHS14.54bn from GHS13.04bn) despite a weaker earnings year
Strong trade finance and diaspora banking capabilities
keyRisks: FY2025 profitability fell sharply versus a strong FY2024: net operating income down to GHS1.46bn (from GHS1.97bn) and PAT down to GHS286.5m (from GHS536.9m) — EPS fell from GHS3.09 to GHS1.65
Parent (Access Bank Nigeria) managing its own large acquisition debt
Rapid balance-sheet growth alongside falling profitability warrants monitoring capital ratios
ACCESS.GH.analystNote: FY2025 marks a notable earnings step-down after a peak FY2024: net operating income and PAT both fell by roughly a quarter to a half, even as deposits and the balance sheet kept growing. Proposed dividend GHS0.6241/share. managementRating softened from 'Strong' to 'Average' to reflect the earnings decline. roe, roa, currentRatio and debtToEquity are carried over from stale data, not reverified.

keyStrengths: Corporate banking focus with quality clients
Profit after tax has grown roughly 5x since FY2022, reaching GHS551.3m in FY2024 (+30% YoY)
FY2024 dividend raised sharply to GHS0.34/share (from GHS0.05)
keyRisks: MATERIAL: Société Générale Group has confirmed an active strategic review of its Ghana unit and engaged Lazard to find a buyer, as part of a wider SocGen Africa divestment wave (subsidiaries in Burkina Faso, Mozambique, Cameroon, Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Mauritania are being sold or already sold) — a change of majority owner in Ghana is a live, unresolved risk as of August 2026
Small market share; low liquidity on GSE
Ownership uncertainty could affect strategy and capital support during a transition
SOGEGH.GH.analystNote: FY2024 audited results show continued strong recovery: net profit GHS551.3m (+30%), revenue ~GHS1.35bn, dividend raised to GHS0.34/share. The dominant story, however, is corporate: SocGen Group's planned Ghana exit (reported since mid-2024, engaging Lazard, still not finalised as of Aug 2026) creates real ownership-change risk that outweighs the improving fundamentals for now. EPS, shares outstanding, currentRatio, ROE, ROA and debtToEquity were not found in public sources this cycle and are carried over from stale data — treat as approximate.

keyStrengths: Dramatic FY2025 turnaround ("resurrection"): PBT swung from a GHS225.1m loss in 2024 to a GHS580.8m profit; PAT rose to GHS367.2m from GHS35.1m
Capital Adequacy Ratio improved from -3.15% to 27.17% following a successful recapitalisation — among the strongest capital positions on the GSE
GHS381.4m in non-performing loan recoveries during 2025
Government development mandate — agriculture sector focus with large rural branch network
keyRisks: Agriculture-sector lending carries structurally higher credit risk
Government ownership can lead to politically-influenced lending decisions
No dividend declared yet — track record of shareholder returns still needs to be established post-recapitalisation
ADB.GH.analystNote: FY2025 is a genuine inflection point: total revenue rose to GHS1.73bn, PBT to GHS580.8m and PAT to GHS367.2m, while the Capital Adequacy Ratio swung from -3.15% to 27.17% after a recapitalisation exercise. ROE (~19.3%) and ROA (~2.2%) are both derived from disclosed profit and equity/asset figures and represent a marked improvement, though not yet at par with GCB or Ecobank Ghana. No dividend has been declared. managementRating upgraded to 'Strong' to reflect the turnaround execution; currentRatio and debtToEquity are carried over from stale data, not reverified.

keyStrengths: Debuted on the GSE via an oversubscribed IPO on 19 December 2025 (~GHS786m raised) — the first new GSE listing in 7 years, improving capital access and public disclosure
FY2025: operating income +19% to GHS1.30bn, PAT +43% to GHS482.9m, EPS up to GHS1.43 from GHS1.00
Growing loan book in SME and retail segments; net interest income nearly doubled to GHS962m
keyRisks: Non-performing loans reportedly remain elevated despite the strong profit growth
Newly public — limited multi-year track record as a listed company
Smaller balance sheet limits large corporate deals
FAB.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (Deloitte-audited) results are record results: operating income GHS1.30bn, PAT GHS482.9m (+43%), EPS GHS1.43, final dividend GHS0.29/share (~GHS100m total, up from GHS0.22/GHS75m in 2024). The December 2025 IPO materially changed the shareholder base and share count; sharesM here (~338m) is derived from netProfit/EPS rather than directly sourced. roe, roa, currentRatio and debtToEquity are carried over from stale data, not reverified.

keyStrengths: Backed by Republic Financial Holdings (Trinidad) — Caribbean banking expertise
Focus on mortgage and home finance (formerly HFC Bank)
Two consecutive years of 30%+ profit growth (FY2024 PAT +45%, FY2025 PAT +37% to GHS288M) under 'Republic Verse' digital transformation strategy
keyRisks: Small market share in competitive Ghanaian banking sector
Mortgage lending exposed to Ghanaian property market softness
ROE, current ratio and debt/equity not independently reverified this update — treat with caution despite strong headline profit growth
RBGH.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (audited, AGM April 2026): PAT GHS287.94M (+37% YoY), PBT GHS440.29M (+34%), EPS GHp32.50 (+37%), total assets GHS12.33B (+29%). Proposed dividend GHS0.05/share. Shares outstanding corrected to ~886M (previous entry substantially understated share count, which distorted per-share economics). Clear multi-year turnaround from post-DDEP weakness; ROE/leverage metrics not directly reverified this cycle.

keyStrengths: Libyan Arab African Investment Company backing (foreign capital)
Confirmed profitable and dividend-paying: D340M profit FY2024 (+31% YoY), regular interim + final dividends now confirmed for 2024 and 2025
keyRisks: Correction: this bank (The Gambia) reports in Gambian Dalasi (GMD), not GHS as the old entry implied — cross-border currency risk complicates comparison for GHS-based investors
Very low GSE trading volume/liquidity
Geopolitical/regulatory risk from Gambian domicile
FY2025 full-year audited figures not yet located; only a D0.35/share interim dividend (Nov 2025) confirms continued profitability
TBL.GH.analystNote: Major correction from prior entry: TBL is headquartered in and reports in Gambian Dalasi (GMD), not GHS. FY2024 (year ended Dec 31, 2024): net interest income D946.8M, PBT D463.2M (+27%), profit for year D340.1M (+31% YoY), EPS D1.70. Shares outstanding corrected to ~200M (was 490M) based on cross-checked market cap and dividend data. An interim dividend of D0.35/share was declared for FY2025 (Nov 2025), suggesting continued profitability, but full FY2025 audited results were not found in this search. Revenue figure is an approximation (net interest income only; fee/commission income not disaggregated in sources found).

keyStrengths: Pan-African presence across 35 countries — unique diversification
Leading pan-African digital banking and payments platform (Omni Plus)
Record FY2025 profitability: ROTE 27.8%, cost-to-income improved to 48.3%, dividend reinstated after a three-year pause
keyRisks: Exposure to multiple African currency devaluations simultaneously
Complex holding structure makes analysis difficult
Asset-quality pressure flagged in FY2025 results as a constraint on further growth (per analyst commentary)
Operating in some high-risk jurisdictions (West/Central Africa)
ETI.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (audited, released ~March 2026): net revenue $2.45B (+17%), PBT $801M (+21%), profit attributable to ETI shareholders $407M (+22%), ROA 1.9%, ROTE 27.8% (record). Shares outstanding corrected to ~23.7B (was 29.5B). Dividend reinstated after a three-year pause, though exact per-share amount not confirmed (old dps figure retained as placeholder). ROE, debt/equity and current ratio not independently reverified.

keyStrengths: Ghana's largest insurance conglomerate (Enterprise Life + Enterprise Insurance)
Record FY2025 insurance revenue of GHS1,745.6M (+10% YoY)
Strong brand and distribution network across Ghana
keyRisks: FY2025 profit dipped slightly YoY (GHS352.8M vs GHS366.5M in 2024) on insurance-side headwinds, cushioned by a strong investment-income year — underlying trend worth monitoring
Insurance penetration in Ghana remains low
Currency risk on USD-denominated reinsurance premiums
EGL.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (audited, published April 2026): Insurance revenue GHS1,745.6M (+10%), Profit After Tax GHS352.8M (down modestly from GHS366.5M in 2024) — insurance-side headwinds partly offset by an investment-income windfall. EPS GHS1.277, proposed final dividend GHS0.164/share. ROE ~21%, ROA ~8% (both derived from reported equity/assets). Shares outstanding corrected to ~276M (was 500M). Still the best-in-class GSE insurer; FY2025 shows the first profit dip in recent years but revenue growth continued.

keyStrengths: Government ownership provides franchise security
Strong FY2025 turnaround: PAT surged 57% to GHS84.05M; capital adequacy ratio 222.68% vs 150% regulatory minimum
keyRisks: State-owned — prone to political/bureaucratic decision-making
A one-off gain from land regularisation at Greenhill boosted FY2025 profit — underlying run-rate profitability likely lower going forward
Audit reportedly flagged some subsidiary liability concerns (per MyJoyOnline coverage)
Still less commercially focused than private-sector peer EGL
SIC.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (audited): insurance revenue GHS598.2M (+7%), PAT GHS84.05M (+57% YoY, aided by a one-off land-regularisation gain at Greenhill plus improved investment income), EPS ~GHS0.43, dividend GHS0.1022/share (~GHS20M total, subject to NIC approval). ROE ~11% (derived), capital adequacy 223%. Shares outstanding corrected to ~196M (was 1,140M) based on dividend/EPS cross-check. Genuine improvement vs historically weak results, but one-off gains inflate the headline growth rate — EGL remains the preferred GSE insurance pick.

keyStrengths: Wilmar International subsidiary — world's largest agribusiness conglomerate backing
Prime agricultural land in Wenchi (Brong-Ahafo region)
FY2025 revenue +6% to GHS369.0M on strong CPO/CPKO prices; EPS GHS2.42, dividend GHS1.30/share
keyRisks: Commodity price risk — crude palm oil (CPO) price fluctuations
Climate/weather risk on crop yields
Wilmar could delist or buy out minority shareholders
BOPP.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (audited, published April 2026): revenue GHS369.0M (+6%), profit for year GHS84.5M, EPS GHS2.4202, proposed dividend GHS1.3047/share. Shares outstanding corrected to ~34.8M (confirmed issued-share count) — previous entry's 125M figure was significantly overstated, which understated true per-share value. Still one of GSE's strongest-fundamentals stocks: high margins, consistent dividends, low leverage, Wilmar backing.

keyStrengths: Strategic asset — processes Ghana's key export commodity (cocoa)
Government support likely given national importance
keyRisks: Chronically loss-making — high energy and processing costs
High leverage — financial distress risk; equity reported negative in FY2024 commentary despite a 2023 COCOBOD debt-to-equity conversion

Losses reportedly widened further into FY2024/FY2025 (revenue down, losses up per USD-denominated coverage) with no confirmed turnaround as of mid-2026 ('faces 15% loss amid Ghana expansion plans', May 2026 headline)
Government ownership leads to inefficiency
Volatile cocoa bean prices compress margins
CPC.GH.analystNote: No confirmed GHS-denominated audited figures newer than FY2023 could be verified this update, so core numeric fields are UNCHANGED from the prior entry — do not treat as current. Later coverage (stockanalysis.com, BFT, citinewsroom, FX Leaders) reports figures in USD only: FY2024 revenue ~$31.1M (-3.6%), net loss ~$13.1M (widened ~13%); nine months to June 2025 revenue -27% YoY to $16.2M with a $10.2M loss; a May 2026 headline still describes an active loss amid an expansion push. Directionally this confirms the company remains deeply loss-making with no turnaround evident, but currency/scale could not be reconciled to GHS with confidence, so figures were not updated. CPC's fiscal year ends September 30. Speculative only — avoid for regular investment.

keyStrengths: Iconic consumer brands (OMO, Sunlight, Lipton, Close-Up) with strong recall
FY2025 profit surged 65% to GHS95.7M on revenue growth to GHS1.04B — strong standalone performance post-Unilever-Global divestiture, cash balance reportedly doubled
Wide distribution network across Ghana
keyRisks: Margin compression risk from forex-linked input costs (palm oil, chemicals) remains structural even as recent results improved
Intense competition from importers and local brands
Longer-term brand-license/supply-chain dependency on Unilever Global following the local divestiture
UNIL.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (audited): revenue GHS1,039.2M (+12%), net profit GHS95.7M (+65%), operating profit GHS143.3M, EPS GHS1.5273 (+64%), proposed dividend GHS1.00/share (sharply higher than prior years). Shares outstanding corrected to ~62.5M (was 188M, a significant overstatement that distorted per-share metrics). Post-divestiture standalone performance has been notably strong — margins improving from previously thin levels. ROE/ROA/leverage not independently reverified this cycle.

keyStrengths: Market leader in frozen dairy (ice cream, Fan Ice, Fan Milk) in Ghana
FY2025 revenue +46% to GHS1.0B, net profit +36% to GHS67.4M — strong growth momentum, EBITDA ~GHS124.9M
Strong brand loyalty across all income segments
keyRisks: Margins compressed by rising electricity costs (cold chain critical)
Forex impact on milk powder and packaging imports
Danone Group has been divesting brands globally — divestiture risk, though recent results have not visibly suffered
FML.GH.analystNote: FY2025 (audited, published early 2026): revenue GHS1,000.7M (+46%), net profit GHS67.4M (+36%), operating profit GHS96.1M, EPS GHS0.58 (+36%), final dividend raised to GHS0.11/share. Share count refined to ~116M (close to prior 124M estimate). Strong growth year on robust cold-chain/dairy demand; ownership-transition risk noted previously has not visibly hurt performance. ROE/ROA/leverage not independently reverified this cycle.

keyStrengths: Diageo brand portfolio (Guinness, Malta Guinness, Smirnoff, Baileys)
FY2025 (year ended June 30, 2025) was a record year: revenue up 52% to GH¢3.59bn and net profit up roughly 10x to GH¢346m
Beer sales crossed 50% market share for the first time in over a decade; outlet coverage grew from 35,000 to 42,000
Largest dividend payout in 7 years (GH¢0.098/share, GH¢30.1m total)
keyRisks: Excise duty increases squeeze margins on beer/spirits
Consumer purchasing power constrained by inflation
Competition from cheaper imports and local brewers (AB InBev Ghana)
Forex-linked raw materials (malt, hops) erode margins
Unaudited Q1 FY2026 (three months to Sept 30, 2025) showed revenue down ~14-16% y/y, suggesting the FY2025 surge may be moderating
GGBL.GH.analystNote: Major turnaround year: FY2025 (June year-end) revenue and profit both surged sharply, with record profit and the highest dividend in 7 years. However, unaudited quarterly filings for FY2026 (three months to Sept 2025) already show a revenue decline and profit pressure from 'transition costs,' so the FY2025 spike should not be extrapolated blindly. Balance-sheet ratios (current ratio, ROE, ROA, debt/equity, operating margin) are estimated from limited data and not directly confirmed from the full financial statements — treat with caution. Moderate-to-improving risk profile pending confirmation of FY2026 trajectory.

keyStrengths: Niche printing and stationery business with established clients
FY2025 revenue up 31.5% to GH¢36.97m and profit up ~27% to GH¢3.26m, driven by local and export sales growth
Resumed paying a dividend (GH¢0.086/share for FY2025) after previously paying none
H1 2026 (six months to June 2026) profit up a further 19% to GH¢2.61m, showing continued momentum
keyRisks: Extremely small company — very low trading volume on GSE (only ~6.8m shares in issue)
Digitisation reducing demand for printed materials
Illiquid — difficult to buy or sell
Auditor (Baker Tilly) flagged inadequate narration in the company's ledgers despite an unmodified opinion
CMLT.GH.analystNote: Micro-cap printing company with extremely low trading volume, but financials have materially improved: FY2025 revenue and profit both grew strongly and the company reinstated a dividend. Actual shares in issue (~6.83m) are far lower than previously modeled (45m), which changes per-share metrics substantially. ROE/ROA/debt-to-equity are derived from limited balance-sheet snippets (total equity ~GH¢7.46m) and should be treated as approximate. Free cash flow direction not independently confirmed — carried over as unverified.

keyStrengths: Local food brand with distribution in key Ghanaian markets
Returned to profitability in FY2025 (net profit ~GH¢265,000) after a loss in FY2024, driven by a new supply arrangement with Unifa Brothers
Cash position improved materially (GH¢115,145 at year-end vs GH¢1,003 prior year)
keyRisks: Company is far smaller than previously modeled — actual FY2025 total income was only ~GH¢1.62 million, not the ~GH¢50m previously assumed; treat prior scale entirely as an error
Extremely illiquid on GSE
Intense FMCG competition from larger players
No dividend declared for FY2025
Turnaround is very recent (one profitable year after a loss) and driven largely by a single new supply contract
SAMBA.GH.analystNote: IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the previous dataset's revenue figure (~GH¢50m) appears to have been badly wrong — actual audited FY2025 total income was only ~GH¢1.62 million with net profit of ~GH¢265,000, a swing from a ~GH¢245,000 loss in FY2024. This is an extremely small, illiquid company; EPS, current ratio, ROE/ROA, debt-to-equity and share count could not be verified from available sources and are carried over from the old (likely unreliable) dataset — treat all fields beyond revenue/profit as low-confidence placeholders.

keyStrengths: Merger of Dannex and Ayrton Drug (two established Ghanaian pharma companies)
FY2025 revenue up 9.8% to GH¢190.16m; operating profit up 52% and net profit up 37.6% to GH¢14.32m
Total equity up 53.5% to GH¢41.08m, with retained earnings flipping from a GH¢6.30m deficit to a GH¢8.02m surplus
Manufacturing capability for generics — import substitution play amid growing local demand
keyRisks: Import competition from cheap Indian and Chinese generics
Forex exposure on active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs)
Regulatory compliance costs for GMP standards
FY2025 figures found were labeled unaudited/preliminary in some sources — final audited numbers may differ slightly
Actual shares in issue (~84.7m, derived from EPS) is well below the previously assumed 250m, materially changing per-share economics
DASPHARMA.GH.analystNote: Continued structural improvement: revenue, operating profit and net profit all grew in FY2025, and the balance sheet moved from an accumulated deficit to a retained-earnings surplus. Dividend per share and current ratio could not be reverified this cycle and are carried over from the prior dataset — treat as unconfirmed. Healthcare remains a secular growth theme for Ghana; medium risk given thin margins and import competition, but trend is positive.

keyStrengths: Niche manufacturer of IV fluids — essential, non-cyclical healthcare product
Relatively low domestic competition for IV manufacturing
Pursuing a GH¢50m rights issue and private placement to fix working capital and fund capital projects
keyRisks: FY2025 swung to a significant net LOSS of GH¢4.63m (from a GH¢0.64m loss in FY2024) as revenue nearly halved to GH¢9.30m (from GH¢24.94m) amid working capital constraints and debt-servicing strain limiting raw-material imports
Heavy dependence on public sector (Ministry of Health, hospitals) procurement, with delays hurting cash flow
Very low GSE trading volume
Actual shares in issue appear far higher (~274m, derived from loss-per-share) than the previously modeled 100m, diluting per-share metrics
IIL.GH.analystNote: Materially deteriorated since the old dataset: FY2025 was a loss-making year with revenue collapsing due to working-capital constraints preventing timely API/raw-material imports, and the company is now running a GH¢50m rights issue/private placement to shore up liquidity. Risk has clearly increased versus the prior (already cautious) assessment. Current ratio, ROA and debt-to-equity could not be precisely reverified and are carried over or roughly estimated — treat with caution pending the completed rights issue.

keyStrengths: Ghana's largest indigenous petroleum marketing company (GOIL = Ghana Oil)
Largest retail fuel station network in Ghana
FY2025 net profit rose 7% to GH¢90.67m despite revenue declining from GH¢20.36bn to GH¢18.55bn
First dividend increase in three years (GH¢0.060/share, ~GH¢23.5m total); total group assets grew to GH¢4.88bn
New venture (African Bitumen Terminal Ltd, with Societe Multinationale De Bitumes) diversifies revenue streams
keyRisks: Razor-thin net margins typical of fuel retail (well under 1%)
Petroleum price regulation by NPA can squeeze margins
Forex exposure on crude oil import costs
Current ratio appears to have dipped below 1 (current liabilities have been running ahead of current assets through 2025), a tightening from the prior 1.1x
EV transition (very long-term risk in Ghana context)
GOIL.GH.analystNote: CORRECTED SCALE: prior dataset's revenue figure (GH¢7.8bn) was far too low — actual FY2025 revenue was GH¢18.55bn (down from GH¢20.36bn in FY2024), consistent with GOIL's true scale as a multi-billion-cedi fuel wholesaler/retailer. Net profit grew modestly to GH¢90.67m and the dividend was raised for the first time in three years. Debt-to-equity is carried over from the old dataset — total liabilities/equity is much higher (~3.9x) but that includes trade payables and inventory financing typical of fuel wholesalers, not narrowly comparable 'debt.' Still a reasonable income pick given national strategic importance; medium-low risk.

keyStrengths: TotalEnergies (French major) parent — global best practices and capital
FY2025 (year ended Dec 31, 2025) profit after tax rose 9.3% to GH¢319.08m (from GH¢291.92m), despite revenue declining from GH¢6.14bn to GH¢5.60bn
Premium positioning (higher margin lubricants and specialty fuels) — operating profit rose to GH¢514.5m
Strong corporate and aviation fuel contracts; total dividend per share of GH¢3.2245
keyRisks: Global parent TotalEnergies could delist from GSE
Thin fuel retail margins; NPA price regulation
Forex exposure on crude imports
Current liabilities exceeded current assets at year-end 2025 (a 'managed position' per the company, backed by credit lines) — a genuine liquidity watch-item
Shares in issue appear far lower (~112m, derived from EPS/profit) than the previously modeled 282m — this materially changes per-share metrics and should be confirmed against the share register
TOTAL.GH.analystNote: Revenue corrected down slightly from the old estimate (GH¢6.5bn) to a confirmed GH¢5.60bn for FY2025, with profit growth continuing (+9.3%) on a much higher EPS (GH¢2.85) than previously modeled — largely explained by a far smaller confirmed share count (~112m vs 282m assumed). ROE/ROA/debt-to-equity are now grounded in sourced balance-sheet totals (equity GH¢552.6m, total liabilities GH¢1.12bn) but the debt-to-equity figure reflects total liabilities, not narrowly-defined interest-bearing debt. Consistent dividend, international backing; low-medium risk, though the share-count correction and negative working capital position warrant a follow-up check against the primary annual report.

keyStrengths: ZEN Petroleum completed a fully-subscribed IPO and listed on the GSE on April 22, 2026, raising GH¢640m (128m new shares at GH¢5.00)
Ranks among the top 4 Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) in Ghana, supplying ~49% of fuel to the mining sector
FY2025 revenue was GH¢6.34bn (up from GH¢5.11bn in FY2023) with profit of GH¢436.7m and gross profit nearly doubling to GH¢780m
Rapidly expanding retail network of 63+ active stations nationwide
keyRisks: No dividend track record yet as a newly-listed company
Newly public — limited governance/disclosure history for GSE investors to evaluate
Fuel retail is inherently thin-margin and exposed to NPA price regulation
Current ratio, ROE, ROA and debt-to-equity could not be verified post-IPO and are carried over from the prior (pre-IPO-context) dataset — likely stale
ZEN.GH.analystNote: MAJOR REVISION: ZEN Petroleum turns out to be a substantially larger and more established company than the old dataset suggested — a top-4 Ghanaian OMC that just completed an oversubscribed IPO (listed April 2026), with FY2025 revenue of GH¢6.34bn and net profit of GH¢436.7m, not the small GH¢1.2bn/GH¢20m thin-margin operator previously modeled. EPS is derived using the post-IPO enlarged share capital (640m shares) since a pre-IPO count wasn't directly sourced. Risk profile should be reassessed upward in quality (established scale, mining-sector supply relationships) but downward in certainty (no listed dividend or governance history yet, balance-sheet ratios unverified).

keyStrengths: Operator of Ghana's Jubilee and TEN offshore oil fields; Jubilee Petroleum Agreement extended to 2040 (ratified Feb 2026), adding long-term certainty
FY2025 free cash flow was positive at $99m and net debt reduced to $1.35bn (from $1.45bn)
Non-core asset divestment programme delivered $347m from Gabon/Kenya sales, aiding deleveraging
TEN FPSO acquisition agreed (Feb 2026, $205m gross) consolidating control of Ghana infrastructure
keyRisks: FY2025 revenue fell sharply to $847m (from $1.29bn) and production declined to 40.4 kboepd (from 51.4 kboepd), partly reflecting asset disposals but also field maturity

On a continuing-operations basis the company posted a loss of ~$129m (basic loss per share ~$0.08); a small headline group profit of $7m for the year was driven by one-off gains on the Gabon/Kenya divestitures, not underlying profitability
Still heavily leveraged: net debt of $1.35bn against a much smaller equity/profit base
Dividend remains suspended with no clear reinstatement timeline
TLW.GH.analystNote: USD-denominated. FY2025 headline group profit was a small $7m, but this masks a ~$129m loss from continuing operations — the positive headline was driven by one-off divestment gains (Gabon, Kenya). Revenue and production both declined materially from the old dataset's figures, confirming the 'declining Ghana production' risk already flagged. Net debt reduced modestly and free cash flow stayed positive, and the Jubilee licence extension to 2040 is a genuine long-term positive, but this remains a speculative, high-risk holding pending sustained profitability on a continuing-operations basis. Dividend still suspended.

keyStrengths: Tier 1 global gold miner with assets across Africa, Americas and Australia; NYSE-primary listing gives global institutional access
FY2025 was an exceptional year: revenue surged 71% to $9.9bn and profit for the period nearly tripled to $3.17bn, driven by the gold price surge (safe-haven demand)
Record free cash flow of $2.9bn (tripled y/y); Adjusted EBITDA up 129% to $6.3bn
Record $1.8bn in dividends declared for 2025 (357 US cents/share total, up sharply from prior years) — 62% of free cash flow
keyRisks: Gold price sensitivity — earnings would fall sharply if gold prices retreat from current highs
Operational risk in high-risk jurisdictions (DRC, Mali, Guinea)
Rising energy and labour costs at mines
Shares in issue appear to have grown materially (~611m, derived from EPS/profit, vs ~415m previously assumed) — dilution should be confirmed against the official share register
Ghana GSE cross-listing remains secondary — limited local trading depth relative to NYSE
AGA.GH.analystNote: FY2025 results (global, consolidated — not just Ghana operations) were exceptional across the board, driven by the gold price supercycle: revenue, profit, free cash flow and dividends all surged. ROE/ROA are rough estimates (equity base not directly sourced this cycle) and should be treated as directional only; debt-to-equity is carried over from the prior dataset (balance sheet is described as strong with manageable debt, but not independently reverified this cycle). A quality gold major offering direct leverage to gold prices; medium risk (essentially gold-price risk) given how much of the 2025 upside was cyclical.

keyStrengths: Owner and operator of Bibiani Gold Mine in Ghana's Western Region — producing asset with FY2025 (11 months to Dec 31, 2025) revenue of ~$483M, up from ~$459M prior year
Gold equivalent production of 146,571 oz for the period, supported by Russell satellite pit start-up and Bibiani plant upgrades (oxygen plant, shear reactor)
Listed on CSE (Canada) and GSE — dual market visibility
Realized gold price rose to ~$3,372/oz, capturing the 2025-2026 gold bull run
keyRisks: Reported a large net loss of roughly $345M for the FY2025 period (vs. $62M loss prior year), driven by AISC blowing out to ~$3,902/oz (from ~$2,168/oz) and financing/non-cash charges tied to an August 2025 'Financing Package'
Share count has roughly tripled since the placeholder baseline (from ~270M toward 750-900M by mid-2026) — material shareholder dilution
Balance sheet leverage from mine acquisition and growth financing remains elevated
Operational cost control at Bibiani has deteriorated sharply — execution risk
USD reporting currency — GHS investors face FX exposure
ASG.GH.analystNote: Asante Gold Corporation (ASG) operates the Bibiani Gold Mine in Ghana (acquired 2022) and changed its fiscal year-end to December 31; the FY2025 report covers the eleven months ended Dec 31, 2025. Revenue held up (~$483M) on higher gold prices and volumes, but AISC cost overruns plus financing-related charges drove a large net loss (~$345M, EPS -$0.55) versus the prior year's smaller loss — a materially worse profitability picture than the old $150M revenue/$18M profit placeholder implied. Share count has grown substantially through 2025-2026 financing activity; sharesM (765) is an approximate mid-2025 figure and likely understates the FYE count somewhat — treat as directional. Not a dividend payer. Higher risk/reward than established Ghanaian miners; watch Q1 2026 update (quarter ended March 31, 2026) for whether cost/AISC trends are improving.

keyStrengths: Depositary share exposure to AngloGold Ashanti global operations (GSE ratio: 1 ordinary share : 100 GhDS)
FY2025 was an exceptional year for AGA: revenue up 71% to $9.9B, profit nearly tripled to $3.17B, EPS $5.19, and the balance sheet swung to a net cash position (~$879M) from net debt
Record $1.8B in dividends declared for 2025 (357 US cents/ordinary share, ~62% of free cash flow), directly benefiting GhDS holders on a scaled-down basis
Free cash flow tripled to a record ~$2.9B
keyRisks: Depositary shares add a layer of complexity over direct shares
Very low liquidity on GSE (~GHS 41M market cap for the GSE-listed depositary line)
Tracking error vs. primary NYSE/JSE listing
Results are gold-price-driven — a large share of the 2025 surge reflects the gold price rally rather than structural operational gains, so normalization risk exists if gold pulls back
AADS.GH.analystNote: American Depositary Shares of AngloGold Ashanti listed on GSE (share code AAD/AADS, ratio 1 ordinary : 100 GhDS). FY2025 group results were exceptionally strong on the back of high gold prices — revenue, profit, EPS, FCF and dividends all surged versus 2024's already-solid year. Figures above are full AngloGold Ashanti group results (same convention as GLD.GH), not scaled to the GhDS ratio. Balance-sheet ratios (current ratio, ROE, ROA, debt/equity, operating margin) were not found in this pass and remain unverified/null. Complex instrument with thin GSE trading — for local exposure to AGA, prefer AGA.GH directly.

keyStrengths: Gold Fields operates Tarkwa (Ghana) and Damang — historically two world-class mines; FY2025 group revenue surged 68% to $8.75B and attributable profit rose to $3.57B ($3.99/share) on higher gold prices and 18% production growth to 2.44Moz
Adjusted free cash flow up 391% to ~$2.97B; net debt reduced to ~$1.05B
Final dividend raised sharply (total annual payout ~$1.59/share) plus $353M in additional shareholder returns (special dividends + buybacks)
South African primary listing with global investor base
keyRisks: Ghana government rejected Gold Fields' Damang mine lease renewal in April 2025 and took operational control of the facility — a material, realized loss of a Ghana asset, not merely a risk
At Tarkwa, five of six mining leases expire April 2027; Gold Fields submitted its renewal application in November 2025 — outcome still pending and a key Ghana political/regulatory risk
Gold price sensitivity — a large share of the 2025 profit surge reflects elevated gold prices rather than structural cost improvement
South Africa JSE primary listing — currency conversion complexity for GHS investors
Balance-sheet ratios (current ratio, ROE, ROA, debt/equity, operating margin) carried forward from prior estimates and not reverified this cycle
GLD.GH.analystNote: USD-denominated. Gold Fields GDR gives exposure to one of Africa's best-managed gold miners, now delivering record profitability on the 2025-2026 gold price rally. However, the Ghana-specific picture has deteriorated: Damang's lease was rejected and the government took control of it in 2025, and Tarkwa's lease renewal (5 of 6 leases, due April 2027) remains undecided. Revenue/profit/EPS/dividend figures above are freshly verified for FY2025; balance-sheet ratios are unchanged prior estimates. Medium-high risk given the Ghana asset-base uncertainty despite strong group financials.

keyStrengths: IT services in a growing digital economy — Enhanced Payment Service Provider, systems integration and outsourcing
'Smart Source' service line grew 1,587% in FY2025 (off a small base)
keyRisks: Micro-cap with essentially zero trading volume
Profit after tax fell sharply to GH¢0.46M in FY2025 (from GH¢3.95M in FY2024) due to planned investment in operations and technology; total assets declined to GH¢15.8M from GH¢19.9M
No dividend recommended for FY2025
Competition from large global tech companies entering Ghana
Very limited financial disclosure
CLYD.GH.analystNote: Near-dormant micro-cap IT/payments company. FY2025 revenue was roughly flat (GH¢23.6M vs GH¢23.9M) but profit slumped ~88% to GH¢0.46M (EPS ~GH¢0.0137) as the company invested in operations and technology; no dividend. Share count (~34M) derived from EPS/profit and differs from the prior placeholder (55M) — treat as approximate. Essentially untradeable due to zero market volume. No strong financial rationale for investment at current stage. Avoid.

keyStrengths: Digital media/signage/event-planning niche — revenue grew 16.7% YoY to GH¢0.82M in FY2025 on event planning, advertising and digital production services
keyRisks: Extremely small, essentially illiquid
Losses widened in FY2025 (loss before tax GH¢0.52M vs GH¢0.35M in FY2024; loss after tax GH¢0.55M) despite revenue growth — rising operational costs are outpacing sales gains
No dividend, persistent net losses
Limited competitive differentiation
DIGICUT.GH.analystNote: Micro-cap digital media/production company. Audited FY2025 results (published April 2026) show revenue of just GH¢0.82M — far smaller than the prior placeholder's GH¢15M guess — with a widening net loss of GH¢0.55M (EPS -GH¢0.0047). ROE/ROA and operating margin are not meaningfully disclosed for a loss-making micro-cap of this size and are left null rather than carrying forward stale positive figures. Essentially untradeable. No investment case for most investors.

keyStrengths: Holds Ewoyaa Lithium Project — one of Africa's highest-grade hard-rock lithium deposits; received key Ghana regulatory approvals in 2025 (Mine Operating Permit, EPA Environmental Permit, Land Use Certificate, Water Use Permit)
Annual losses roughly halved to ~A$6.6M in FY2025 (from ~A$12.65M in FY2024) via cost cuts (voluntary executive pay cuts, workforce rationalization)
Binding Scheme Implementation Deed signed with Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt to acquire 100% of Atlantic Lithium for US$210M cash, payable at closing — a concrete takeout offer, not just an offtake partner
Listed on ASX (ALL/A11), AIM/LSE and GSE — broad international investor access
keyRisks: Pre-production exploration company — zero revenue, negative cash flow (cash used in operations ~$4.9M in FY2025, down from ~$9.1M)
Cash position fell to A$5.39M at FY2025 year-end (from A$12.68M) — thin runway pending the Huayou transaction closing

Huayou acquisition (both of Atlantic Lithium directly and of Elevra's separate Ewoyaa interest for ~US$71M) is not yet closed — expected around Q1 FY27 — and remains subject to approvals/conditions; deal could still fall through or be repriced
Lithium price collapse (2023-2025) has severely depressed developer valuations generally
AUD-reporting currency creates FX complexity for GHS investors
ALLGH.GH.analystNote: Atlantic Lithium Limited (listed as ALLGH on GSE) is developing the Ewoyaa Lithium Project in Ghana. The corporate picture has clarified materially since the prior note: Elevra Lithium agreed in May 2026 to sell its separate Ewoyaa interest to Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt for ~US$71M, and — independently — Huayou signed a binding Scheme Implementation Deed to acquire 100% of Atlantic Lithium itself for US$210M cash, expected to close around Q1 FY27. This is effectively a take-private/acquisition situation rather than an open-ended exploration story. FY2025 operating losses narrowed on cost discipline, but cash reserves are thin. Revenue/EPS/dividend fields are little-changed and reconfirmed; balance-sheet ratios (current ratio, ROE/ROA, debt/equity) were not reverified this cycle. Speculative — value now hinges heavily on the Huayou deal closing at the agreed terms.

keyStrengths: Holds real estate and investment assets (development, purchase, sale and rental of real estate; equities and fixed-income investments) providing some underlying asset backing
Backed by OAK Partners, an Accra-based private investment services firm
keyRisks: IMPORTANT IDENTITY CORRECTION: the previous dataset entry for MAC.GH described an automotive/industrial distribution business with government clients — that description does not match the company actually trading as MAC.GH today, which is Mega African Capital Limited, an investment/real-estate holding company. Prior numeric fields (revenue ~GH¢180M, profit ~GH¢12M) appear to have been fabricated or misattributed and have been replaced/nulled rather than carried forward

Persistent and widening losses: net loss of GH¢33.7M in FY2024 (vs GH¢30.8M in FY2023), driven almost entirely by very high finance costs (~GH¢32.8M) against negligible revenue (GH¢0.32M, itself down from GH¢0.46M)
Net loss vastly exceeds revenue, making margin ratios not meaningful — a sign of a heavily leveraged or distressed capital structure
Extremely low liquidity/almost no trading volume on GSE
Balance-sheet detail (shares outstanding, equity, assets/liabilities) could not be verified from available sources this cycle
MAC.GH.analystNote: Mega African Capital Limited (MAC.GH) is a long-term investment/real-estate holding company (real estate development/rental, equities and fixed-income investment, brokerage/advisory services), not the automotive distributor described in the prior stale entry — that appears to have been a data error. FY2024 shows a tiny revenue base (GH¢0.32M) swamped by large finance costs (~GH¢32.8M), producing a GH¢33.7M net loss that widened from GH¢30.8M in FY2023. Given the identity correction and highly leveraged/distressed profile, most ratio fields are left null rather than carrying forward numbers for the wrong company. No confirmed GSE annual report newer than FY2024 was found (earlier internal hint pointed to a stale FY2019 filing for a different 'MAC' entity — likely Mechanical Lloyd, ticker MLC, delisted 2021 — which is a separate, unrelated company). Treat this as a high-risk, thinly-traded, financially distressed micro-cap.

keyStrengths: Provides career-oriented post-secondary education, diploma and degree programmes via Meridian Pre-University — a recurring, tuition-type revenue model
Total operating income roughly doubled YoY to GH¢3.09M (FY ended July 31, 2025, from GH¢1.22M in FY2024) with gross profit of GH¢0.98M
Net loss narrowed to GH¢0.30M in FY2025 from GH¢0.46M in FY2024 — improving trend
keyRisks: IDENTITY CORRECTION: the prior entry described MMH.GH as a diversified distribution conglomerate; the company actually trading as MMH.GH is Meridian-Marshalls Holdings, an education-services provider. Prior numeric fields (revenue ~GH¢280M, profit ~GH¢18M) appear fabricated/misattributed and have been replaced/nulled
Still loss-making despite revenue growth — high administrative and director-remuneration costs relative to scale
Very low GSE liquidity, effectively untradeable
Non-calendar fiscal year (ends July 31) with very small absolute scale limits reinvestment capacity
Limited public financial disclosure constrains verification of most balance-sheet ratios
MMH.GH.analystNote: Meridian-Marshalls Holdings Limited (MMH.GH) operates in post-secondary/vocational education (Meridian Pre-University), not the distribution conglomerate the prior stale entry described — that appears to have been a data error, and prior placeholder figures have been corrected rather than carried forward. FY2025 (year ended July 31, 2025) shows operating income nearly doubling to GH¢3.09M with the net loss narrowing to GH¢0.30M, a positive trend off a very small base. No dividend. Shares outstanding, EPS and most balance-sheet ratios could not be verified this cycle and are left null; total assets were roughly flat at GH¢8.59M.

keyStrengths: Real estate assets in Ghana are structurally valuable long-term
Rental income provides some revenue stability

FY2025 (unaudited) marked a sharp turnaround: revenue surged to GH¢5.64M from GH¢0.25M in 2024, and the company swung from a GH¢0.57M net loss to a GH¢0.16M net profit, with operating profit reversing from a GH¢0.59M loss to a GH¢0.22M gain
keyRisks: Very small real estate company — even after the FY2025 surge, absolute profit remains minimal (~GH¢0.16M, EPS ~GH¢0.00) on ~115M shares
Extremely low GSE trading volume
Reported alongside 'widening cash flow pressures' despite the revenue/profit turnaround — cash generation lagging reported profitability
Turnaround is based on unaudited FY2025 figures, subject to potential audit adjustment
Ghana real estate market still exposed to currency devaluation and high mortgage rates
No dividend, limited financial disclosure
HORDS.GH.analystNote: Micro-cap real estate company with very limited GSE presence. Unaudited FY2025 results (year ended Dec 31, 2025) show a real turnaround — revenue up over 20x to GH¢5.64M and a swing to a small net profit (GH¢0.16M) after a loss in 2024 — but the absolute scale remains tiny and cash flow commentary was reported as under pressure despite the topline gain. Balance-sheet ratios (current ratio, ROE/ROA, debt/equity) are carried forward from prior estimates and not reverified this cycle. Essentially untradeable; watch for the audited FY2025 statements to confirm the turnaround holds.
